questions.q: In 'The Goose and the Golden Egg', why did the Countryman kill the Goose?
choices: He wanted to get all the golden eggs at once
The Goose had stopped laying any golden eggs
He was very hungry and wanted a goose dinner
The Goose had bitten him on the hand that day
questions.evidence: he could get all the golden eggs at once by killing the Goose

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Goose and the Golden Egg'?
choices: Those who have plenty want more and so lose all
A goose is worth far more than any golden egg could be
Always sell your eggs at the market in town
Be patient and gentle with all your animals
questions.evidence: Those who have plenty want more and so lose all they have.

questions.q: In 'The Fighting Bulls and the Frog', why was the old Frog afraid?
choices: The beaten Bull would run into the marsh and trample them
The Bulls would come and eat all the Frogs
The marsh was drying up in the summer sun
The young Frog wanted to go and fight the Bulls himself
questions.evidence: we shall all be trampled into the mud

questions.q: In 'The Mouse and the Weasel', why could the Mouse not get out of the basket?
choices: He had eaten so much corn he was too big
The Weasel was blocking the hole in the basket
The basket had been tied shut with string
He was stuck fast in the sticky corn
questions.evidence: he became about three times as big around the middle

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Mouse and the Weasel'?
choices: Greediness leads to misfortune
Weasels make the best friends
Baskets are dangerous places
Always help those in trouble

questions.q: In 'The Farmer and the Snake', what did the Snake do after the Farmer warmed it back to life?
choices: It bit the Farmer
It thanked the Farmer
It slid into the field
It fell asleep again
questions.evidence: bit the man who had been so kind to it

questions.q: In 'The Sick Stag', why did the Stag starve to death?
choices: The visiting Animals ate all his food
He was much too sick to eat anything
He could not find any food in the forest
A Lion came by and took all his food
questions.evidence: helped themselves freely to the Stag's food

questions.q: In 'The Goatherd and the Wild Goats', why did the Wild Goats refuse to join the flock?
choices: He treated his old Goats badly and would do the same to them
They did not like the dark cave where he kept all of his flock
He gave them too little food and they were very hungry
They were afraid the storm would never come to an end
questions.evidence: We know how you would treat us later on

questions.q: What is the lesson of 'The Goatherd and the Wild Goats'?
choices: Do not treat old friends badly for the sake of new ones
Wild animals can never be tamed, no matter how kind you are
Always feed your animals well when there is a storm
Stay inside the cave on stormy days and do not go out
questions.evidence: It is unwise to treat old friends badly for the sake of new ones.
